A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ControlG and provide readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices. The retained material can be reliably matched despite figure renumbering, relocation, and added analyses.

before.justification: V1 reports original node-classification, link-prediction, clustering, ablation, timing, and training-diagnostic results in Section 5 and Appendix D.

after.justification: V2 retains these empirical results and adds backbone and task-pool sensitivity experiments in Tables 10–11, alongside expanded diagnostics.

M1.justification: The sensing, log-hypervolume planning, PID scheduling, and five pretext objectives remain unchanged. The allocation-floor formula documents f_min already present in v1's Tables 4–5. Schematic and initialization corrections reconcile descriptions with existing equations and Algorithm 2 rather than establish a different procedure.

E1.justification: Reported evaluations retain the same nine datasets and three downstream tasks. Coauthor-Physics disappears from setup prose but had no dataset or result-table entries in v1. New sensitivity tests use existing datasets and subsets of the existing pretext pool; heterogeneous-graph experiments remain absent.

E2.justification: The retained comparisons contain the same methods. The new GAT experiment reuses Uniform, CAGrad, and Random under another backbone. GCN/GAT are correctly described as backbones instead of supervised comparators; neither version reports separate supervised GCN/GAT result rows.

E3.justification: V2 adds GAT-backbone and K=3/4 task-pool evaluation configurations. Table 4 specifies an ogbn-arxiv controller-grid exception to the previously stated general grid, although selected settings remain unchanged. Link-prediction reporting is narrowed from ROC-AUC and AP to ROC-AUC. These changes do not establish reruns of the retained benchmark experiments.

E4.justification: Appendix D.10 substantially expands robustness analysis with backbone and task-pool sensitivity tests and a qualitative report of 10,283 successful configurations. Figures 4 and 9 add objective-loss/allocation diagnostics, pairwise conflicts, and schedule entropy; Figure 8 expands state diagnostics to Cora and Chameleon. Existing component ablations remain.

E5.justification: V1 Figure 5 describes mean and standard deviation across seeds; v2 Figure 7 instead shows rolling mean and rolling standard deviation within one representative Cora run. New Tables 10–11 report five-seed means without intervals. Retained benchmark tables preserve five-seed 95% confidence intervals, with no reported increase in repetitions.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark, ablation, and timing values in Tables 1–2 and 6–9 are unchanged. V2 adds supplementary GAT and smaller-pool results, including 80.56% Cora accuracy with GAT and 80.14% with K=3, plus expanded diagnostic findings. Section 5.2 corrects top-two classification coverage from eight to nine datasets, consistent with unchanged Table 1.

T1.justification: Theorem C.5 replaces the incorrect dimension-independent bound -1 < d_k(m) < 1 with -(K-1) < d_k(m) < 1. V2 replaces the lower-bound proof with a zero-sum argument and reports a K=8 counterexample to the earlier claim. Appendix B.5 also formally defines the allocation floor. The principal spectral and hypervolume proofs remain.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: feedback-controlled temporal allocation, spectral/interference sensing, Pareto-aware planning, PID execution, and strong downstream performance. The introduction's added emphasis on random scheduling promotes a finding already discussed in v1.

C2.justification: V2 corrects diagnostic explanations: Rayleigh quotient measures scale-invariant roughness, and difficulty tempers allocation rather than increasing it. Starvation guarantees are qualified probabilistically. Appendix D.10 adds substantive applicability limits concerning similar objectives, pretext-pool quality, tested encoders, and untested heterogeneous graphs, including the near-tie with Uniform on Wiki-CS.

D1.justification: V2 fills documentation gaps with task defaults, including masking ratio, contrastive temperature and neighborhood size, decorrelation-head settings, and METIS partition count. It also specifies evaluation details, encoder search ranges, the ogbn-arxiv grid exception, and allocation-floor implementation. These disclosures refine the existing setup; selected configurations and hardware reporting remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The same distinct prior works and overall research positioning are retained. Consolidating duplicate Guo references and updating MVGRL bibliographic metadata do not introduce or remove research works.

P1.justification: The main narrative and section sequence remain largely intact. V2 adds a conflict-of-interest disclosure and Appendix D.10, revises several explanatory paragraphs and cross-references, consolidates implementation discussion, and updates publication text. This is localized editing rather than extensive rewriting.

P2.justification: Visual presentation is substantially reworked: the motivation figure is split, existing clustering ranks gain a chart, runtime bars become horizontal with a logarithmic axis, and diagnostics are replaced or expanded. New diagnostic panels and Tables 10–11 accompany substantial relocation of retained displays. These changes go beyond pagination and renumbering.

improvement.justification: V2 improves reliability by repairing the max-deficit theorem, correcting mechanism explanations, supplying missing settings, and stating meaningful limitations. Sensitivity experiments add useful corroboration. The net gain is limited by mean-only new tables, an unquantified PID-robustness assertion, and the new Figure 5 caption's overstated Cora speedups: Table 9 implies about 2× over CAGrad, not the claimed 5–15×.
